title: Streak an agar plate in four quadrants with a fresh inoculating loop for each, crossing the last streaks
instruction: Streak the plate for isolated colonies, using a new loop for each quadrant: with the first loop, drag through the drop and streak quadrant 1; then with a fresh loop each time, streak quadrants 2, 3 and 4 in turn, each starting with a few strokes that cross the streaks of the quadrant before. Don't dig into the agar. Put each used loop in the discard tray.
context: Laboratory research automation: the four-quadrant streak is how microbiology, clinical and research labs isolate a pure culture, done by hand many times a day. The CDC's training: with plastic loops, take a new loop before each quadrant and discard it after; each new loop starts by crossing the previous quadrant's streaks, the only bacteria it carries, so the culture thins to single colonies by quadrant 4. The difficulty is physical: four times, a slim loop held like a pen must glide its 4.5 mm ring over soft agar with almost no force and find and cross thin streaks. Video: bottom left, a demo-only streak record (loop 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green, 4 purple; colours meeting = crossings).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), same layout every trial. Agar plate: Fisherbrand FB0875712 polystyrene Petri dish base (100 x 15 mm style; 92 mm outside, 88 mm inside, 13.5 mm tall) holding 20 mL of set LB agar (1.5 % agar), 3.3 mm deep, room temperature, no surface water; centred at (34.0, -6.0) on the table, held by double-sided tape under the dish, lid off for the trial, set aside inner face down. Agar poured the day before, stored lid-down at 4 C, warmed to room temperature 1 h before the trial. Underside marked in black marker with a cross through the centre (one line along x, one along y) into quadrants 1 (far right, x > 0 and y < 0 from the plate's centre), 2 (far left), 3 (near left) and 4 (near right), numbered by 1-4 dots near the rim, and a filled blue dot 5 mm across where the drop goes, 1.6 cm forward of and 1.4 cm right of the plate's centre. Sample: a 10 uL drop of an Escherichia coli K-12 culture (e.g. MG1655, biosafety level 1) grown 16-18 h at 37 C in LB broth, shaking, pipetted onto the blue dot with a 2-20 uL pipette just before the trial. Loops: four sterile disposable 10 uL inoculating loops, polypropylene, 200 mm long, 3.6 mm handle, ring 4.5 mm across (MTC Bio M4025 or Heathrow Scientific 03-448-345), laid out from their pack onto a sterile sheet (autoclaved white paper, 24 x 15 cm, centred at (30.0, -21.75), corners taped), flat along x with their rings towards the robot, side by side 3.5 cm apart (ring centres 2.2 cm in from the sheet's near edge; the first 2.25 cm in from its left long edge): ring centres at (20.2, -16.5), (20.2, -20.0), (20.2, -23.5), (20.2, -27.0), butts 19.8 cm further forward. Discard tray: autoclavable polypropylene biohazard tray lined with an autoclave bag (an open stand-in for a sharps biohazard container), 25 x 18 cm, 4 cm deep, centred at (16.0, 5.0), long side along x, taped down. Both arms start in their ready pose, grippers open; nothing else on the table.
scoring: Read from the incubated plate and the trial video. After the trial the plate is lidded and incubated upside down at 37 C for 18-24 h; colonies grow only where a ring rested on the agar, and a cut shows as a groove. Photo from above on a light box beside a mm ruler; lengths measured along the growth lines (a thread along curves). A streak is a line of growth along a stroke, or a row of colonies no more than 5 mm apart along it (first to last colony). A camera films the plate from above during the trial (phone on a stand about 30 cm up, 1080p, 30 fps). Loops are numbered by when they first touch the agar (plate camera): loop k streaks quadrant k. A crossing is a stroke of loop k through loop k-1's growth: a growth line running out of loop k-1's growth (often a lawn in quadrants 1-2) into quadrant k (crossing the marker line where there is no previous growth does not count, and leaves the quadrant bare). Each quadrant starts by crossing: a fresh loop carries no bacteria until it passes the drop (loop 1) or first crosses the previous streak, so what it draws before then grows nothing and doesn't count. Isolated colonies off the streaks (airborne contaminants) are ignored. 0 if the agar is gouged anywhere (a groove or cut on the light box; the gouge check in the reset notes confirms a 0.29 N drag shows and a 0.05 N one doesn't) or a gripper touches it. Otherwise 0.25 per quadrant in turn, stopping at the first that fails: Q1: loop 1 passes the drop, then draws at least 40 mm in quadrant 1; Q2: fresh loop 2 crosses loop 1's streaks at least twice and draws at least 30 mm in quadrant 2 after its first crossing; Q3 and Q4 likewise (loop 4 never touching quadrant 1). Loop k may touch only quadrants k and k-1 (within 2 mm of the line counts as on it): straying into a later quadrant ends the credit before that quadrant, into an earlier one before its own; an old loop back on the agar after a newer one ends it after the quadrants begun (one loop throughout: at most 0.25). At most 0.25 if a later loop touches the drop; at most 0.75 until every used loop lies in the discard tray, let go. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: A fresh marked agar plate with a new drop of the culture, four fresh sterile loops and a fresh autoclaved sheet under them every trial; the plate is labelled with its trial number, lidded and incubated for scoring (plates from many trials incubate together), then autoclaved with the used loops in the tray's bag. BSL-1 culture: gloves and lab coat; wipe the bench with 70 % ethanol before laying out the sheet and after. Once per session, check the gouge readout on a spare plate: a spare loop's ring dragged 2 cm under a 30 g weight (0.29 N) must leave a groove on the light box, under 5 g (0.05 N) none. The drop is pipetted just before the trial starts.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX at 240 Hz. Dish and agar fixed; the 0.3 mm sterile sheet is drawn, not simulated. Each loop (listed size, 1.6 g) is a handle and, on a sprung hinge (0.1 N at the ring bends it 3 mm), its neck and ring. The agar doesn't deform: it is streaked where a ring rests on it with 0.01 N or more; over 0.25 N (gel strength over the ring's patch) is a gouge. No bacteria: the streak record stands in for growth, counted only after a loop passes the drop or crosses the previous streak.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (3,600 steps; the right arm turned towards the loops and the plate and came close to the loops but never grasped one; the left arm stayed near its start; nothing was touched); demo: 1.0
